title: GPU throughput arithmetic: FLOPS, memory bandwidth, SIMD and SIMT
status: reviewed and locally validated; independent round 2 ACCEPT
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Both assigned transcripts were read completely and all 26 listed frames inspected. No complete independent audio review was performed. Corrections are supported by viewed numerical slides and actual primary references, not a claim that garbled transcription faithfully represents speech.

The original GTX 1660 board datasheet was not retrieved. Its 192-bit/2001 MHz example is interpreted as a lecture arithmetic model consistent with approximately 8 Gb/s effective rate and 192 GB/s, not an independently verified board specification or a verified internal-clock signaling identity.

The exact local memory-clock-to-effective-pin-rate convention was not established. The chapter reports cudaDevAttrMemoryClockRate and bus width without multiplying them into an asserted RTX 3050 Laptop memory peak.

CUDA online guides were retrieved as current documentation, with pages served as 13.4; installed headers and version metadata were CUDA 13.3.1, nvcc 13.3.73. The property query uses attributes because installed cudaDeviceProp clock members were removed. No claim of version identity is made.

The whitepapers were read from actual downloaded PDFs shared read-only under work/ch17-sol and independently extracted into this private chapter directory. V100 is August 2017 v1.1; A100 is v1.0 copyright 2020; GA10x bytes are v2.1 despite the V1 URL filename. One initial A100 web-open timed out; direct local PDF inspection, rather than the failed web extraction, supports its cited passages.

Tensor numerical rates are model calculations using the dated enabled products, dense or explicitly structured-sparse-equivalent work and stated clocks. No Tensor kernel was benchmarked, and the cancellation exercise uses an explicitly idealized nearest TF32 input conversion rather than asserting every library mode.
The three-stage scalar/vector pipeline is a checked ideal simulation with one-cycle stages, full-width operand supply and no stalls. It is not a CPU SIMD or GPU instruction-latency measurement.

Four sequential memory/FMA captures ran in an exclusive slot. Device power, temperature, dynamic clocks and background services were not controlled. Reported peak-clock attributes and a separate idle clock are not sampled kernel clocks; the 82.4 percent ratio is relative to the stated model, not a certified absolute utilization.

Effective bandwidth counts source-level requested bytes, not DRAM hardware-counter traffic. Arrays were already device-resident, so results do not measure PCIe, NVLink, a NIC or inter-node communication. The empirical arithmetic-intensity comparison combines two microbenchmarks and is not a measured physical roofline.

Exact floating-point comparisons are justified only by the deliberately binary-exact test values and bounded recurrence. Full payload checks passed, but do not establish numerical accuracy for arbitrary FP32 inputs or correctness for every architecture.

The final structured checker reran the five complete printed contracts once. Its variable timing samples are verification evidence and are excluded from the four-capture ranges. Later prose-only cleanup preserved the complete parsed executable fingerprint exactly.
lecture_corrections: A 4x4 bare matrix product has 64 multiplies and 48 adds, 112 operations. Matrix accumulation AB+C has 64 FMA-equivalents, conventionally 128 FLOPs. The slide listing four multiplies plus three adds but labeling four operations per output is interpreted as four FMA-equivalents, not four individual FLOPs.

A100 table entries 64 FP64 and 512 TF32 FMA-equivalents per SM per cycle are throughput quantities, not physical Tensor-core counts; the enabled product has four Tensor cores per SM, 108 SMs and 432 total.

The GDDR/HBM table reverses the numerical interface-width comparison and conflates per-chip with per-stack units. HBM2 uses 1024 bits per stack in these examples; no universal latency/capacity ordering follows.
RTX 2080 in the actual GA10x table uses GDDR6/NRZ rather than GDDR6X/PAM4; a quoted effective bit rate must not be multiplied again for DDR or PAM4.
The GTX clock is 2001 MHz, about 2 GHz, rather than 2 MHz. Its rounded bandwidth is not an exact equality with every printed clock digit.

160 blocks across 80 SMs is an arithmetic average of two, not a guarantee of uniform simultaneous residency. Logical thread identities do not identify persistent physical CUDA cores; PTX explicitly warns diagnostic smid may change after preemption.
